claim_id.description:
Client-generated idempotency fence. New controllers should always set
this; omission preserves the original V1 one-shot claim behavior.

complete.description: False while the command may still append more chunks.

stdin.description: Bounded, non-secret bytes delivered to the guest process's stdin.

timeout_secs.description:
Maximum time the command may run before the executor kills it and
reports a timeout failure. Clamped to
`(0, MAX_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS]` by `queue_command`; `None`/omitted
falls back to `DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

idle_ttl_seconds.description:
See `Sandbox::idle_ttl_seconds`. Server-side default/clamp config
(`SANDBOXWICH_DEFAULT_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS` /
`SANDBOXWICH_MAX_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS`) applies when this is omitted or
exceeds the operator-configured ceiling.

max_lifetime_seconds.description:
See `Sandbox::max_lifetime_seconds`. Server-side default/clamp config
(`SANDBOXWICH_DEFAULT_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS` /
`SANDBOXWICH_MAX_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS`) applies when this is omitted
or exceeds the operator-configured ceiling.

secret_ref_ids.description:
Secret references to deliver to this sandbox as read-only files. Each
id is resolved in the caller's own tenant scope at create time; an
unknown, revoked, or foreign reference fails the create rather than
producing a sandbox that silently lacks a credential.

CreateSecretRefRequest.description:
`deny_unknown_fields` is load-bearing: it is what makes "the control plane
cannot be handed raw credential bytes" a contract rather than a
convention. A client that tries to send `value`/`data` is rejected by the
extractor itself, before any handler runs (422 `invalid_request`).

ForkSnapshotRequest.description:
Complete child configuration for restoring directly from a durable
snapshot. Fields needed to provision the child are intentionally required
so this request does not depend on the source sandbox still existing.

max_lifetime_seconds.description:
See `Sandbox::max_lifetime_seconds`. Restoring a sandbox from a
snapshot is a sandbox-creation path like `create`/`fork`, so it goes
through the same server-side default/clamp.

MaestroHostedRunnerActivationIdentityReq.description:
The exact identity tuple presented by an authenticated Maestro runner.
Sandboxwich resolves the remaining binding fields from its authoritative
resident, placement, and lease rows in the same transaction as validation.

MaestroHostedRunnerActivationValidationB.description:
One authoritative binding and durable proof returned by the combined
identity validation endpoint. The binding is resolved and the proof is
committed under one database transaction, so callers do not need a
preceding connection-binding read.

MaestroHostedRunnerActivationValidationR.description:
Authenticated Maestro rendezvous activation presented by Platform for
validation against Sandboxwich's current resident, placement, and lease
authority. `activation_id` is the idempotency/replay fence; every remaining
field must exactly equal the live connection binding.

Durable point-in-time receipt that Sandboxwich accepted one exact Maestro
activation tuple while its authoritative generation and lease were live.

authorityRevision.description: Versioned monotonic generation vector for the authority snapshot.

tupleDigest.description:
Versioned digest of the exact authoritative tuple consumed by
Platform's activation CAS.

tupleSha256.description: Legacy request-only digest retained for compatible replay detection.

MaestroHostedRunnerConnectionBindingResp.description:
Non-secret connection and certificate binding for a live, tenant-scoped
Maestro hosted runner. Callers use the exact URI SAN to authenticate the
server certificate issued by Identity; every component is fenced to the
same live provider placement and lease.

MemoryLimit.description:
Memory tier.

`Serialize`/`Deserialize` are implemented by hand below in terms of
[`DbVariant`], so the wire values are `1g`/`4g`/`16g`/`64g` rather than the
Rust variant names. `utoipa::ToSchema` derives from the variant identifiers
and cannot see a hand-written `Serialize`, so each variant carries an
explicit `#[schema(rename = ...)]`. Without them the exported OpenAPI
document advertises `OneG`/`FourG`/... and any consumer generating a client
from it sends values this type rejects.
`memory_limit_schema_matches_serialized_values` pins the two together.

replaceTerminal.description:
Explicitly replace an authoritative terminal resident at
`expected_generation`. Live or leased residents always reject this.

idle_ttl_seconds.description:
Rolling idle window: if no activity is observed for this many
seconds, the background expiry sweeper stops the sandbox the same way
`max_lifetime_seconds` does. `None` (the default) disables idle
reaping. "Activity" is the most recent of this sandbox's own last
lifecycle-state transition, its most recently queued guest command,
and `last_activity_at` (SSH access, desktop access, and resident-
process observations all bump it, throttled -- see
`docs/capabilities.md`).

last_activity_at.description:
Server-maintained, throttled "last seen doing something" timestamp,
separate from `updated_at` (which only moves on lifecycle-state
transitions). Bumped by SSH access, desktop access, and resident-
process observation requests -- see `docs/capabilities.md` for the
full list and the throttle window. Not caller-settable; absent from
`CreateSandboxRequest` on purpose. `None` until the first bump (or
forever, for a sandbox never touched through any of those surfaces).

max_lifetime_seconds.description:
Hard cap on how long this sandbox may stay outside `Archived`,
measured from `created_at`. `None` (the default) means no cap. The
background expiry sweeper drives an expired sandbox through the same
`stop_sandbox` path a user-initiated stop uses once this deadline
passes, regardless of activity.

ttl_seconds.description:
Retention window for an *already-`archived`* sandbox's record: how
long its row (and dependent rows) stay queryable after teardown before
`run_cleanup_controller` deletes them. Does **not** govern how long a
live sandbox may run -- see `max_lifetime_seconds` and
`idle_ttl_seconds` for that. The three knobs are independent and
commonly all set on the same sandbox; see `docs/capabilities.md` for
the full distinction.

SandboxObservedState.description:
Provider-facing projection used by external control planes to reconcile a
sandbox without depending on the full tenant-visible Sandbox resource.

secret_mounts.description:
Resolved secret deliveries for this sandbox. Locators only; the worker
turns each one into a read-only CSI volume mount.

SandboxRuntimeProfile.description:
Closed runtime trust profiles. The APEX profile permits only the trusted
image supervisor to start as uid 0; it is not a tenant-controlled root
toggle and guest mission processes still run as uid 10001.

SandboxSecretMount.description:
Resolved, material-free delivery instruction handed to a worker through
the provisioning job payload. Every field is a locator: there is nothing
here to redact because there is nothing secret here.

envFileVariable.description: Environment variable the guest reads the path (not the value) from.

filePath.description: Path of the delivered file inside that directory.

mountDir.description: Read-only directory the worker must mount the delivery volume at.

SecretBackend.description:
Where the secret *material* actually lives. Sandboxwich stores a
reference to it and never reads, transports, or persists the bytes.

`csi_secret_provider_class` names a `SecretProviderClass` the operator has
provisioned for the tenant. The kubelet's Secrets Store CSI driver reads
the material from the external store and mounts it into the Pod's tmpfs
directly, so no plaintext copy is ever created in a Kubernetes `Secret`
object, in etcd, or in any sandboxwich process. The class name is
tenant-supplied; its namespace never is, because a tenant-chosen namespace
would be a cross-tenant read primitive.

SecretDelivery.description:
How the material reaches the sandbox. `file` is the only supported mode:
a read-only file mounted under [`SANDBOX_SECRET_MOUNT_PREFIX`].

Argv delivery is deliberately absent (visible in `/proc/*/cmdline`), and
so is delivering the value in an environment variable; the guest receives
only the *path* through `<NAME>_FILE`-style variables (see
[`SecretRef::env_file_variable`]).

SecretRef.description:
A durable, tenant-scoped reference to long-lived user or model credentials.

`tenant_id` is the platform organization; `workspace_id` narrows it
further. Both are part of every read, bind, and delete path, so a
reference is invisible and unbindable outside its own scope.

SecretSource.description:
Typed locator for externally held secret material. Carries no value field
on purpose, in any direction: the control plane must not be able to accept
raw credential bytes even by accident.

objectKey.description: File the class writes the material to inside the CSI mount.

objectName.description:
Name of the `SecretProviderClass` in the operator-owned secret
namespace.

SterileCellClaimLocatorV1.description:
Non-secret locator returned only to the worker that owns a sterile cell.
The raw lease attestation and its stored digest are deliberately absent.

cleanup_pending.description: True while the pool membership durably requires a provider cleanup retry.

provider_absent.description: True only after the pool membership records an exact provider-stop completion.

SterileCellRuntimeClass.description:
Closed isolation classes admitted to the one-shot sterile-cell pool.
`KataMicrovm` preserves the VM boundary. `GvisorLowerRisk` is a distinct,
explicitly signed class and cannot satisfy a Kata claim.

agent_image.description:
Digest-pinned image containing the exact sandboxwich-agent binary copied
into the candidate's shared executable volume.

maestro_image.description: Digest-pinned Maestro image executed only after sterile activation.

service_name.description: Stable pre-created Service identity for the candidate Pod.

SterileResidentActivationV1.description:
One-shot authority for activating a resident inside a purpose-created
sterile cell. The attestation is a bearer secret and must only travel in
the bounded resident-bootstrap handoff.

ValidateMaestroWorkloadIdentityRequest.description:
Internal Identity-to-Sandboxwich live placement validation. This is not a
bearer exchange: the caller must already be the authenticated Identity
service, and every field is compared with Sandboxwich's authoritative
resident-process, lease, placement, and observed Pod state.

info.description: HTTP control plane for disposable development sandboxes
info.title: Sandboxwich API

200.description: Current typed command status and exit result
Ordered bounded command output page; complete is true only after terminal status

404.description: Unknown, foreign, or distinctly replayed proof

409.description: Placement fence is no longer live
Placement fence is no longer live
Sandbox is not a ready trusted-supervisor sandbox

post.summary:
Runner-host (evalops/platform `rust/services/runner-host`) is the only
caller of this route and mirrors its request/response types by hand. The
route is documented here so that mirror can be validated against the
exported OpenAPI document instead of against itself.

202.description: Command accepted with an Operation resource
Fork accepted with child sandbox and asynchronous operation

200.description: Durable proof of an exact live Maestro activation tuple

409.description: Activation tuple is stale, expired, replayed with different material, or mismatched

200.description: Authoritative binding and durable proof for one exact live Maestro identity tuple

409.description: Activation identity is stale, expired, replayed, or mismatched

200.description: Live tenant-scoped Maestro connection and exact server certificate binding

404.description: No tenant-scoped Maestro hosted runner exists

409.description: The Maestro placement is pending or not live

503.description: Resident process capacity or materialization is pending

parameters.description: Typed resident name; orb-sidecar requires a non-empty bootstrap
parameters.name: name

200.description: Existing resident process returned for an idempotent same-spec request

400.description: Invalid request, including a missing or empty orb-sidecar bootstrap

delete.summary:
Revocation is a state transition, not a delete: the row stays queryable so
an operator can see that a credential reference existed and when it was
withdrawn. A revoked reference can never be bound to a sandbox again.

202.description: Snapshot restore accepted with child sandbox and asynchronous fork operation

200.description: Worker admission closed; typed requests return a durable drain receipt
